## Review

**8 out of 10, Strong.** Presentation quality, judged with the SlideDeck Co review heuristic (https://slidedeck.co/review-methodology/). The ask, the evidence and the merit of the idea are not rated.

Across the 72 pages inspected, almost every chart slide carries a full-sentence headline in the blue bar that states the takeaway (slides 7, 12, 40, 48), with one chart and a clear chart title, so a reader gets the point in seconds. The route is easy to follow: contents (slide 5), blue section dividers (slides 6, 45), and repeated recap slides (slides 16, 29, 60, 62, 66, 68) keep the audience oriented through a very long deck. The visual system is consistent and disciplined, with clean charts, direct labels on slide 12, and a restrained palette. Weaknesses are tiny, near-illegible source notes, faint axis labels, some sparse text-only slides, and a very long run of similar-looking pages that is better suited to reading than to presenting.

**Worth keeping:** Keep the takeaway headline in the blue bar over a single clean chart, the numbered contents slide, and the recap slides that highlight the current point in a list (slides 62, 66, 68).

**Most useful repair:** Enlarge the source notes and the pale axis labels so they can be read at normal size, and fill the near-empty bars on the untitled text slides (slides 10, 13, 29) with a real title or remove the bar.

**What would change the score:** I would trim or merge the run of near-identical tool and product slides in the e-commerce section (slides 49 to 60) and add more variation in layout to break the rhythm.

## Summary

Mary Meeker's Internet Trends 2018 was presented at the Code 2018 conference on May 30, 2018, and published by the venture firm Kleiner Perkins. It opens with a title slide, a credits slide thanking contributors, and a context slide that frames the report around data, personalization, R&D spending, e-commerce, consumer spending, the consumerization of enterprise software, and China. A table of contents then lists twelve sections in order: users, usage, innovation and competition with scrutiny, e-commerce, advertising, consumer spending, work, data gathering and optimization, economic growth drivers, China, enterprise software, and USA Inc. and immigration. Each section opens with a short title slide, followed by charts that each carry one headline claim, such as the flat growth in smartphone shipments and the rise in internet users past half the world's population. The deck is built around data slides with headline-style titles and small-type source notes. Slides worth studying include the smartphone shipment chart that pairs bars with a growth line, the section divider slides, and the contents slide, which uses numbered sections with page references.

## Questions about this deck

**How many slides does the Mary Meeker, Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2018 deck have?**

The deck is listed as having 295 pages. The slides supplied for this review are numbered through slide 38.

**What sections does the Mary Meeker, Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2018 deck cover?**

The table of contents on slide 5 lists twelve sections, from Users (pages 5-9) through USA Inc. + Immigration (pages 278-291). The sections in order are Users, Usage, Innovation + Competition + Scrutiny, E-Commerce, Advertising, Consumer Spending, Work, Data Gathering + Optimization, Economic Growth Drivers, China, Enterprise Software, and USA Inc. + Immigration.

**What does the Mary Meeker, Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2018 deck say about smartphone shipments?**

Slide 7 is titled 'Global New Smartphone Unit Shipments = No Growth @ 0% vs. +2% Y/Y' and charts global shipments against year-over-year growth from 2009 to 2017. Slide 6 frames the section as 'Internet Devices + Users = Growth Continues to Slow'.

**What does the Mary Meeker, Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2018 deck say about internet users?**

Slide 9 is titled 'Global Internet Users = 3.6B @ >50% of Population (2018)' and charts internet penetration from 2009 to 2017. Slide 4 states that at 3.6B, the number of Internet users has surpassed half the world's population.

### Slide 4

**Text**

Context
We use data to tell stories of business-related trends we focus on. We hope others take the ideas, build on
them & make them better.
At 3.6B, the number of Internet users has surpassed half the world’s population. When markets reach
mainstream, new growth gets harder to find - evinced by 0% new smartphone unit shipment growth in
2017.
Internet usage growth is solid while many believe it’s higher than it should be. Reality is the dynamics of
global innovation & competition are driving product improvements, which, in turn, are driving usage &
monetization. Many usability improvements are based on data - collected during the taps / clicks /
movements of mobile device users. This creates a privacy paradox...
Internet Companies continue to make low-priced services better, in part, from user data. Internet Users
continue to increase time spent on Internet services based on perceived value. Regulators want to ensure
user data is not used ‘improperly.’
Scrutiny is rising on all sides - users / businesses / regulators. Technology-driven trends are changing so
rapidly that it’s rare when one side fully understands the other...setting the stage for reactions that can have
unintended consequences. And, not all countries & actors look at the issues through the same lens.
We focus on trends around data + personalization; high relative levels of tech company R&D + Capex
Spending; E-Commerce innovation + revenue acceleration; ways in which the Internet is helping
consumers contain expenses + drive income (via on-demand work) + find learning opportunities. We review
the consumerization of enterprise software and, lastly, we focus on China’s rising intensity & leadership in
Internet-related markets.
3

- Review: Across the 72 pages inspected, almost every chart slide carries a full-sentence headline in the blue bar that states the takeaway (slides 7, 12, 40, 48), with one chart and a clear chart title, so a reader gets the point in seconds.

**Layout**

A full-width solid navy title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide, with the two-line white title left-aligned at about 1.7% from the left edge. A single centred bold chart title sits below the band, followed by one wide chart plot with a left value axis, right percentage axis and a horizontal legend centred beneath it. A thin light rule separates the footer, where the Kleiner Perkins logo sits at the bottom left, the source line is centred, and the page number 6 sits at the bottom right.

**Visuals**

Chart: combined stacked column and line chart titled 'New Smartphone Unit Shipments vs. Y/Y Growth'. Left axis titled 'New Smartphone Shipments, Global' in units of billions of units, range 0 to 1.5B with gridlines labelled 0, 0.5B, 1.0B, 1.5B. Right axis titled 'Y/Y Growth' in percent, range 0% to 90% with labels 0%, 30%, 60%, 90%. X axis categories 2009 to 2017. Stacked columns have three series from bottom to top: Android (dark navy #00517A), iOS (light grey #BFBFBF), Other (teal green #258B74). Column totals are not printed; about values read from the plot: 2009 Android about 0.01B, iOS about 0.02B, Other about 0.14B, total about 0.18B; 2010 Android about 0.07B, iOS about 0.05B, Other about 0.19B, total about 0.31B; 2011 Android about 0.25B, iOS about 0.10B, Other about 0.15B, total about 0.49B; 2012 Android about 0.50B, iOS about 0.14B, Other about 0.09B, total about 0.73B; 2013 Android about 0.80B, iOS about 0.16B, Other about 0.06B, total about 1.02B; 2014 Android about 1.06B, iOS about 0.19B, Other about 0.05B, total about 1.30B; 2015 Android about 1.16B, iOS about 0.24B, Other about 0.04B, total about 1.44B; 2016 Android about 1.24B, iOS about 0.22B, Other about 0.01B, total about 1.47B; 2017 Android about 1.24B, iOS about 0.22B, Other about 0.00B, total about 1.46B. Y/Y Growth line in crimson red (#C8215A approx.) with about values: 2009 about 17%, 2010 about 73%, 2011 about 61%, 2012 about 47%, 2013 about 40%, 2014 about 28%, 2015 about 11%, 2016 about 2%, 2017 about 0%. No points are highlighted. Legend centred below the plot in one row: Android (navy square), iOS (grey square), Other (teal square), Y/Y Growth (red line). ### Slide 12

**Review notes**

- Worth studying: A stacked bar chart colour-codes three device categories and labels each segment, keeping the total readable across ten years.
- Review: Across the 72 pages inspected, almost every chart slide carries a full-sentence headline in the blue bar that states the takeaway (slides 7, 12, 40, 48), with one chart and a clear chart title, so a reader gets the point in seconds.
- Review: The visual system is consistent and disciplined, with clean charts, direct labels on slide 12, and a restrained palette.

**Text**

Digital Media Usage @ +4% Growth... 5.9 Hours per Day (Not Deduped) Daily Hours Spent with Digital Media per Adult User 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 Hours Spent per Day, USA 5.9 5.6 5.4 5.1 4.9 4.3 3.7 3.2 3.0 2.7 3.3 3.1 2.8 2.6 2.3 1.6 0.8 0.4 0.3 0.3 2.1 2.2 2.2 2.2 2.3 2.5 2.6 2.4 2.3 2.2 2.3 2.2 2.2 2.6 0.6 0.4 0.4 0.3 0.3 0.3 0.3 0.4 0.4 0.3 0.2 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 Other Connected Devices Desktop / Laptop Mobile KLEINER PERKINS 2018 INTERNET TRENDS Source: eMarketer 9/14 (2008-2010), eMarketer 4/15 (2011-2013), eMarketer 4/17 (2014-2016), eMarketer 10/17 (2017). Note: Other connected devices include OTT and game consoles. Mobile includes smartphone and tablet. Usage includes both home and work for consumers 18+. Non deduped defined as time spent with each medium individually, regardless of multitasking. 11

**Layout**

Full-width navy header band across the top 12.5% of the slide holds a two-line left-aligned white title starting at about 1.9% from the left edge. **Visuals**

One line chart. Chart type: line chart with a single series. Chart title: WiFi Networks (bold, dark slate). Y axis: title WiFi Networks, Global (rotated 90 degrees, vertical text); scale 0 to 500MM in gridlines every 100MM, labelled 0, 100MM, 200MM, 300MM, 400MM, 500MM; values in millions of networks (MM). X axis: years labelled every two years 2001, 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017; the series runs from 2001 to about 2017/2018. **Layout**

A full-width dark blue title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide with a left-aligned white title. Below it, a centred stack of 'Affirm' over 'Financing' sits above a left-aligned '1,200+ = Merchants' label and a 4 by 2 grid of merchant tiles, with a stove image and cyan '$350' badge beneath on the left. A hollow arrow sits centre-right and points to a phone-screen mockup at the right, which spans roughly 26% to 86% of slide height. A thin footer rule sits near 93% height, with the Kleiner Perkins wordmark bottom-left, a centred source line and the page number bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Eight merchant logo tiles in a 4 by 2 grid with a faint drop shadow. Row 1: DJI logo (white bold wordmark on dark green-black #1F2B25 tile); wayfair (white lowercase wordmark on purple #6B2F6B tile with small multicolour dots over the i); Expedia (blue globe mark and dark blue wordmark on yellow #FFC30B tile); PELOTON (white logo with small 'Visit store ›' text bottom-right on black #111111 tile). Row 2: REBECCAMINKOFF (small dark grey spaced wordmark on white tile); TRADESY (white serif spaced capitals on black #111111 tile); Reverb (orange script wordmark on white tile); JOYBIRD FURNITURE (white bird mark and wordmark on teal #00AFB9 tile). A photograph of a black freestanding gas range with its oven door open and three trays of prepared food on the oven racks, viewed front-on at a slight angle, full-colour against white, lit evenly from the front, shown unboxed with no crop. A solid cyan #00C8E5 circle overlaps the top-right of the range, carrying the white bold text '$350'. A large hollow right-pointing block arrow with white fill and a 2 to 3 pixel cyan #00C8E5 outline. A phone-screen screenshot framed by a thick black border: a back arrow top-left, a three-segment progress bar with the last segment in cyan, 'STEP 3 OF 3' in small grey caps, the approval headline in bold black, grey body copy, and three white rounded cards with light grey borders showing offers in blue, blue and purple text with chevrons. Light grey footer wordmark image of 'KLEINER PERKINS 2018 INTERNET TRENDS' in spaced capitals, bottom-left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white background. Header band #00517A with white Arial regular title. Affirm in bold dark slate #3E464E, Financing in bold mid grey #7F7F7F, Merchants label in bold #3C444C, all Arial bold sans-serif. Title about 4.4% of slide height, labels about 3.7%, source and page number about 1.3% to 1.5%. Accent cyan #00C8E5 for the badge and arrow outline. Merchant tiles are square-cornered with soft shadows. Phone frame has a thick black border and rounded white cards. Footer text in light greys #A6A6A6 and #BFBFBF. No gradients.

**Layout**

A full-width dark blue title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide, with the title left-aligned at about x 2.1% and vertically centred in the band. Below it are two columns: a left column (Intercom phone mockup under a centred two-line heading) and a right column (a line chart under a left-aligned heading), separated by a thin vertical grey rule at about x 50%. A thin light-grey footer rule sits near y 93.5%, with the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, the source line centred in the footer and the page number 56 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Two visuals. (1) Left: a phone-sized screenshot of the Intercom messenger mockup for AboveAVG, boxed by a 2-pixel-looking black border with square corners, placed in the left column centred under the heading. The screen shows an orange-to-coral gradient header with the wordmark ABOVEAVG, the greeting 'Hi, Sally!' and the line 'How can we help?'. Below, a white card reads 'Start a conversation' and 'The team typically replies within 30 minutes.', with two circular avatar photos (a woman with long dark hair and a smiling man in a dark jacket on green backgrounds) and a coral pill button 'New conversation' with a white paper-plane icon. Next is a white card 'Find an answer quickly' with a search field containing 'how' and a coral square button with a white right chevron. The bottom card shows a coral thumbnail reading 'HOW TO BUILD BETTER ONBOARDING' and the text 'Learn how to engage and onboard from the pros' followed by 'Join AboveAVG's Tom and Sam as they outline tried and tested strategies for onboarding new' (cut off by the frame's bottom edge). Image is cropped at the bottom. (2) Right: a line chart titled 'Customer Conversations'. Y-axis: 'Conversations Started, Global', rotated vertical, ticks 0, 100MM, 200MM, 300MM, 400MM, 500MM, horizontal light-grey gridlines at each tick. X-axis: years 2013 to 2018 as labels, one per year, with no unit label. Single series in magenta-red line, about 2013 near 2MM rising slightly to about 15MM in early 2014, about 25MM in 2014, about 55MM at start of 2015, about 100MM in late 2015, about 185MM in early 2016, dip to about 160MM mid-2016, about 200MM in late 2016, about 385MM in early 2017, dip to about 350MM, rising to about 400MM, about 380MM, about 450MM late 2017, ending about 495MM at the 2018 mark. No legend, no data labels, no highlighted points. The chart is printed without numeric values, so all values are estimates.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background with a dark teal-blue title band (#00517A) across the top. Title is set in Arial regular, white (#FFFFFF), about 4.4% of slide height, with the ellipsis. Column headings are Arial Bold: 'Intercom' in dark slate #3E464E and 'Real-Time Support' in mid grey #7F7F7F, both about 3.7% of slide height; 'Customer Conversations' is Arial Bold mid grey #7F7F7F at the same size. Chart tick labels and axis title are Arial Bold, light grey #BFBFBF, about 2.2% of slide height. Chart line is magenta-red about #C2185B, about 3 px wide with square joins. Gridlines are very light grey, about 1 px. Source line is Arial in light grey #BFBFBF at about 1.3%. Page number is Arial in #A6A6A6 at about 1.5%. Divider rule is light grey #D9D9D9, about 1 px. No gradients or shadows on the slide itself; the phone screenshot has its own coral gradient and white cards with soft shadows.

**Visuals**

Five overlapping screenshots, each with a thin dark border and a soft drop shadow, shown as a staircase from upper left to lower right. (1) Organic Search: an early Google BETA homepage with the Google! logo in multicolour letters (blue, red, yellow, blue, green, red) with small BETA beneath, a search box containing 'travel', a '10 results' dropdown, 'Google Search' and 'I'm feeling lucky' buttons, and a results list beneath with the first results marked with red bars and percentages 74% and 71%; the image is on a white background with black and blue text. (2) Paid Search: a Google results page in which the top sponsored ad block and a right-hand sponsored column are outlined with thick rounded red (#D8215A-like) rectangles, the top ad block has a pale yellow fill, and the organic results are blue links on white with small black snippet text. (3) Google Shopping: a Google Shopping results page with a grid of five lawn mower product thumbnails inside a red rounded rectangle, each with a price and small text, and a list of blue text links beneath; the page is white with a light-grey header bar. (4) Product Listing Ads: a mobile-style Google search for 'hairdryer' with a magnifying-glass blue search button, tabs ALL, SHOPPING, IMAGES, VIDEOS, NEWS, and a 'Shop for hair dryers' panel marked 'Sponsored' with brand tabs ALL, CONAIR, REVLON and product images including a mint-green hair dryer, outlined by a thick red rounded rectangle. (5) Shopping Actions: two screenshots side by side: a left Google Assistant chat panel with circular avatars, blue and white text bubbles reading 'OK Google, buy Up & Up laundry detergent', 'Yes, please.', 'I've added it to your Google Express cart.' and 'OK Google, add Up & Up laundry to my shopping list.' with 'Added'; and a right Google Express phone screen showing two product listings with bottle images, prices $6.99 and $6.99, star ratings, 'ADD TO CART' buttons and a red Target icon. The images are flat, uncropped rectangles with no tint or overlay, lit evenly as screenshots. The Kleiner Perkins logo is a small grey image at the bottom left.

**Layout**

A full-width solid navy header band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide, holding a two-line left-aligned white title with a left margin of about 1.9% and the title beginning at about 1.8% from the top. Below it, a single centred bold chart title sits above a line chart that occupies the middle of the slide, with the y-axis on the left (x about 18 to 25%) and the x-axis of quarters and years along the bottom (y about 78 to 84%). A thin grey rule runs across the full width at about 93% height above the footer, with the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, the centred three-line source note in the bottom middle, and the page number 74 at bottom right (x about 96.5%, y about 95%).

**Visuals**

Chart: line chart with a dotted linear trendline. Chart title: 'Facebook E-Commerce CTRs (Click-Through Rates)'. Y-axis: title 'Facebook E-Commerce CTR, Global', unit percent (%), range 0% to 4%, major gridlines at each 1% (labels 0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, 4%). X-axis: quarterly categories Q1 to Q4 for 2016, Q1 to Q4 for 2017, and Q1 for 2018, grouped under year labels 2016, 2017 and 2018 with short grey rules under each group. Single series, solid teal line about 0.5% of slide height thick, with the printed values labelled as follows: 1% at the start (Q1 2016, label sits to the left above the point) and 3% at the last point (Q1 2018, label above the point). The other points carry no printed value; estimates are about 1.3% (Q1 2016), about 1.3% (Q2 2016), about 1.9% (Q3 2016), about 1.7% (Q4 2016), about 1.8% (Q1 2017), about 1.6% (Q2 2017), about 1.8% (Q3 2017), about 2.4% (Q4 2017), and 3% (Q1 2018). Trendline: dotted teal line running from about 1.2% at Q1 2016 to about 2.5% at Q1 2018. Highlighted points: the 1% and 3% endpoints are labelled in bold teal. No legend. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark in grey at bottom left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF with a navy #00517A header band across the top 12.5%. Clean corporate style. Background is plain white. The header band is navy #00517A with white title text. Chart title and axis-free text are dark slate #3C444C. Series line and labels are teal green #258B74. Axis tick labels, quarter and year labels and the axis title are light grey #BFBFBF; the page number is #A6A6A6; the source note is #BFBFBF. Gridlines are pale grey, about #D9D9D9, 0.1% of slide height thick. Typefaces: title is Arial regular (sans-serif) at about 4.4% of slide height; the chart title is Arial Bold at about 3.7%; axis labels, quarter labels and year labels are Arial Bold at about 2.2%; data labels are Arial Bold at about 2.6%; the source note is Arial regular at about 1.3%; the page number is Arial regular at about 1.5%. Shapes are square with no corner radius and no shadows or gradients. Lines are thin and flat.

Left axis: 'Internet Advertising Spend, USA', $ billions, range 0 to $90B, gridlines at $30B, $60B and $90B. Right axis: 'Y/Y Growth', percent, range 0% to 30%, labelled at 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%. Category axis: years 2009 to 2017, one column per year. Printed stack totals above each column: 2009 $23, 2010 $26, 2011 $32, 2012 $37, 2013 $43, 2014 $50, 2015 $60, 2016 $73, 2017 $88. Desktop and mobile split is not printed; about $23B desktop in 2009 rising to about $38B in 2017 (estimates), mobile is the grey remainder above it, thinnest in 2010 and 2011 and largest in 2016 and 2017. Y/Y Growth line has no printed values; about 14.5% in 2010, about 22% in 2011, about 15.5% in 2012, about 17% in 2013, about 16% in 2014, about 20.5% in 2015, about 22% in 2016, about 21% in 2017 (estimates). No line point is printed for 2009. Legend below the axis: dark blue bar 'Desktop Advertising', grey bar 'Mobile Advertising', red line 'Y/Y Growth'. No highlighted points. Gridlines are light grey horizontal lines at 30B, 60B, 90B and a baseline at 0. Photograph or logo: the Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends logo bottom-left, grey.

### Slide 104

**Text**

Personal Saving Rate = Falling @ 3% vs. 12% Fifty Years Ago… / Debt-to-Annual-Income Ratio = Rising @ 22% vs. 15% / Personal Saving Rate & Debt-to-Annual-Income* Ratio / 25% / Debt-to-Annual-Income* Ratio / 20% / Ratio, USA / 15% / 10% / Personal Saving Rate / 5% / 0% / 1968 / 1978 / 1988 / 1998 / 2008 / 2018 / 103 / Source: St. Louis Federal Reserve FRED Database, USA Federal Reserve Bank. *Consumer debt-to-annual-income ratio reflects / outstanding credit extended to individuals for household, family, and other personal expenditures, excluding loans secured by real / estate vs. average annual personal income. Personal saving rate is shown as a percentage of disposable personal income (DPI), / frequently referred to as “the personal saving rate.” (i.e. the annual share of disposable income dedicated to saving)

**Layout**

Full-bleed white slide with a full-width dark teal header band across the top 12.5% holding a two-line left-aligned title, with the chart title centred below it and a single line chart occupying the middle of the slide. A thin light-grey rule separates the footer, which holds the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, a centred source note, and the page number 103 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

One line chart, titled Personal Saving Rate & Debt-to-Annual-Income* Ratio. Y axis: Ratio, USA, 0% to 25% in 5% steps, light grey gridlines, labels in light grey. X axis: 1968 to 2018, labelled every ten years (1968, 1978, 1988, 1998, 2008, 2018). Series 1, Debt-to-Annual-Income* Ratio, crimson #C82055 solid line about 3 pt: starts about 14.7% in 1968, about 15% in 1970s, dips to about 13.2% around 1985, rises to about 16.5% in 1987, about 14.4% in 1992, climbs to about 17.9% in 1997, about 20.5% in 2004, a peak about 22% near 2008 is the highest point near 2008 at about 22%, drops to about 20% by 2011, and ends about 22.5% in 2018. Series 2, Personal Saving Rate, green #258B74 solid line about 3 pt: starts about 12% in 1968, spikes to about 17% near 1973, mostly 8% to 12% through the 1970s and 1980s with a dip to about 3.8% near 1990, about 5% to 8% in the 1990s, a low about 2% near 2005, a spike about 8% near 2007, a spike about 11% near 2014, and ends about 3.4% in 2018. Each series has a dotted linear trendline in its own colour: crimson dotted from about 12.8% to 21.8%, green dotted from about 12.3% to about 3.2%. Series are labelled directly on the chart with no legend; no points are specially highlighted.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF.

**Visuals**

Chart: clustered vertical bar chart titled Relative Household Spending. Y-axis titled Annual Spend, USA, in percent, range 0% to 20%, gridlines and tick labels every 5% (0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%). X-axis categories in order: Shelter, Taxes, Transportation, Food, Household Operations, Pensions* + Insurance, Healthcare, Entertainment, Apparel, Other**. Each category has three bars in series order 1972 (dark blue #00517A, left), 1990 (crimson #C82055, middle), 2017 (teal green #258B74, right) for highlighted categories Food, Entertainment and Apparel; the other categories use three grey bars, light #D9D9D9, mid #BFBFBF and dark #A6A6A6, left to right, with no printed values. Printed values: Food 1972 15%, 1990 15%, 2017 12%; Entertainment 1972 6%, 1990 5%, 2017 4%; Apparel 1972 5%, 1990 5%, 2017 3%. Unlabelled grey bars, estimated: Shelter about 11.8%, 15.4%, 16.8%; Taxes about 15.1%, 9.4%, 14.5%; Transportation about 14.3%, 16.3%, 13.5%; Household Operations about 11.1%, 12.3%, 11.4%; Pensions + Insurance about 6.6%, 8.2%, 10.1%; Healthcare about 4.7%, 4.7%, 6.8%; Other** about 9.3%, 9.1%, 8.1%. **Layout**

Full-width header band across the top with a two-line left-aligned white title; below it a centred bold chart heading over a single line chart with a left price axis, a right market-share axis and a year axis along the bottom. A thin footer rule sits above a footer row with the logo at bottom left, the source note centred and the page number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Line chart titled 'Grocery Price Change Y/Y & Market Share of Top 20 Grocers'. Left axis 'Price Change Y/Y, USA' from -2% to 10% in 2% steps with light grey gridlines. Right axis 'Market Share, USA' from 0% to 75% in 25% steps. Horizontal axis years 1990 to 2017 with labels at 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2017. Series 1, 'Grocery* Price Y/Y Change', dark blue #00517A solid line about 3px wide with a dotted linear trendline in the same blue, sloping down. Approximate values read from the chart, not printed: 1990 about 6.5%, 1991 about 2.6%, 1992 about 0.7%, 1993 about 2.4%, 1994 about 2.9%, 1995 about 3.2%, 1996 about 3.7%, 1997 about 2.5%, 1998 about 1.9%, 1999 about 1.9%, 2000 about 2.3%, 2001 about 3.3%, 2002 about 1.3%, 2003 about 2.2%, 2004 about 3.8%, 2005 about 1.9%, 2006 about 1.7%, 2007 about 4.2%, 2008 about 6.4%, 2009 about 0.5%, 2010 about 0.3%, 2011 about 4.8%, 2012 about 2.5%, 2013 about 0.9%, 2014 about 2.4%, 2015 about 1.2%, 2016 about -1.3%, 2017 about -0.2%. Series 2, 'Top 20 Grocer Market Share', crimson #C00000 solid line about 3px wide with a dotted linear trendline in a lighter crimson, sloping up; it runs from about 1990 at 39% to about 2016 at 67% on the right axis, with about 2001 at 58%, 2008 at 64% and 2016 at 67%, all estimates. The series is labelled by a red text callout 'Top 20 Grocer Market Share' above the line at top right and the blue series by a text label 'Grocery* Price Y/Y Change' under the line at lower left. No legend box. Highlighted points: none marked; the 2008 peak and the 2016 to 2017 drop are the visible extremes. Two logos sit in the footer, see elements.

Shelter as % of Household Spending = 17% vs. 12% (1972)... / Largest Segment in % + $ Growth / Relative Household Spending / 20% / 15% / Annual Spend, USA / 10% / 17% / 15% / 12% / 5% / 0% / Shelter / Taxes / Transportation / Food / Household Operations / Pensions* + Insurance / Healthcare / Entertainment / Apparel / Other** / 1972 / 1990 / 2017 / Total Expenditure / $11K / $31K / $68K / KLEINER PERKINS / 2018 / INTERNET TRENDS / Source: USA Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Consumer Expenditure Survey. *Pensions + Insurance includes deductions for private retirement accounts, social / security, and life insurance. **Other Includes education and miscellaneous other expenses. **Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with a two-line white left-aligned title, starting at about 2% from the left edge. Below it a centred bold chart title over a single clustered column chart occupying the middle of the slide, with a centred legend row near 86% of the slide height, a thin grey footer rule near 93%, and a three-line-plus centred source note in the footer with the logo at bottom left and the page number 116 at bottom right, about 96% from the left.

**Visuals**

Clustered column chart titled Relative Household Spending. Y axis titled Annual Spend, USA, linear scale 0% to 20% in 5% steps with light grey horizontal gridlines at 5, 10, 15 and 20%. X axis categories in order: Shelter, Taxes, Transportation, Food, Household Operations, Pensions* + Insurance, Healthcare, Entertainment, Apparel, Other**, labels rotated about 45 degrees. Three series per category, in left-to-right bar order: 1972 (dark blue #00517A for Shelter, light grey #D9D9D9 elsewhere), 1990 (red #C82055 for Shelter, mid grey #BFBFBF elsewhere), 2017 (green #258B74 for Shelter, dark grey #A6A6A6 elsewhere). Printed values for Shelter only: 1972 = 12%, 1990 = 15%, 2017 = 17%, shown as small data labels above each bar in matching colours. Other values not printed, estimates: Taxes about 15%, 9.3%, 14.5%; Transportation about 14.3%, 16.3%, 13.5%; Food about 15.3%, 14.6%, 11.6%; Household Operations about 11.1%, 12.3%, 11.4%; Pensions + Insurance about 6.6%, 8.2%, 10.1%; Healthcare about 4.7%, 4.7%, 6.8%; Entertainment about 6.3%, 4.5%, 4.2%; Apparel about 5.0%, 5.1%, 2.6%; Other** about 9.3%, 9.0%, 8.1%. **Layout**

A full-width dark blue header band across the top 12.5% of the slide holds a two-line white title left-aligned at about 1.8% from the left edge. Below it, a single chart is centred in the body area with its bold grey chart title centred above the plot. A thin footer zone at the bottom holds the Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends logo bottom-left, a centred three-line source note, and the slide number 120 at the bottom right; no slide-number or footer text appears in the header.

**Visuals**

One dual-axis line chart titled 'Average New Home Square Footage & Residents'. Left y-axis titled 'New Home Square Footage, USA' with ticks 0, 1K, 2K, 3K, 4K (range 0 to 4,000 sq ft). Right y-axis titled 'Residents per Home, USA' with ticks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (range 0 to 4 residents). X-axis shows years 1972 to 2016 labelled every four years (1972, 1976, ..., 2016), with the line running from 1972 to about 2016. Horizontal light grey gridlines (#D9D9D9, thin) at each left-axis 1K step. Series 1, 'New Home Square Footage', is a red (#C00000) line of about 1,650 sq ft in 1972, about 1,750 in 1980, about 2,000 in 1988, about 2,090 in 1992, about 2,260 in 2000, about 2,350 in 2004, about 2,520 in 2008, about 2,400 in 2010, about 2,500 in 2012, about 2,690 in 2015 and about 2,640 in 2016 (values are estimates; the slide prints no data values). Series 2, 'Residents per Home', is a dark blue (#00517A) line of about 3.0 residents in 1972, about 2.88 in 1976, about 2.77 in 1980, about 2.62 in 1988, about 2.65 in 1994, about 2.60 in 2000, about 2.57 in 2004, about 2.57 in 2010 and about 2.53 in 2016 (estimates). Both lines are about 3 pt thick with no markers. No legend; the series are identified by direct coloured labels 'Residents per Home' (blue, upper right, above the blue line near 2008 to 2016) and 'New Home Square Footage' (red, lower left, below the red line near 1976 to 1984). No points are highlighted. Two logos sit in the footer: a stacked Kleiner Perkins logo reading KLEINER PERKINS / 2018 / INTERNET TRENDS in grey, and a KLEINER PERKINS wordmark in grey.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Plain white slide with a dark blue (#00517A) header band. Chart title is bold Arial in dark slate #3C444C at about 3.7% of slide height. Axis titles and tick labels are bold Arial in light grey #BFBFBF at about 2.6% (ticks about 2.2%, x-axis labels about 2.0%). Direct series labels are bold Arial: blue #00517A and red #C00000, about 2.6%. Footer source text is regular Arial #BFBFBF at about 1.3%. Slide number is regular Arial #A6A6A6 at about 1.5%. Line styles: chart series about 3 pt solid; gridlines thin #D9D9D9; a faint light grey hairline separates the footer from the body. No corner radii, shadows or gradients.

**Layout**

Full-bleed white slide with a solid dark-blue title band across the full width at the top (0 to 12.5% of slide height). The two-line title is left-aligned at about 1.9% from the left edge, sitting inside the band. Below it, a single centred clustered column chart fills the middle of the slide, with its chart title centred above the plot and the legend centred below the category labels. The footer is a thin light-grey rule across the slide at about 93.5% height; the Kleiner Perkins logo lockup sits bottom-left at about 1.3% from the left, the source note is centred in the footer, and the page number '124' sits bottom-right at about 95.8% from the left, aligned to the footer baseline.

**Visuals**

One clustered column chart. Chart title: 'Airbnb vs. Hotel – Average Room Price per Night', bold, dark grey #3C444C. Y-axis: 'Price, 1/18' (rotated vertical label, bold, #BFBFBF); tick labels $0 to $350 in $50 steps, bold, grey #BFBFBF, with light grey horizontal gridlines at each tick from $0 to $350. Y range $0 to $350, linear, US dollars. X-axis categories left to right: New York City, Sydney, Tokyo, London, Toronto, Paris, Moscow, Berlin. Two series per category: Hotel (light grey #D9D9D9 columns, placed first in each pair) and Airbnb (dark blue #00517A columns, placed second). Labelled values, Hotel: New York City $306, Sydney $240, Tokyo $220, London $217, Toronto $193, Paris $167, Moscow $118, Berlin $114. Labelled values, Airbnb: New York City $187, Sydney $191, Tokyo $93, London $179, Toronto $114, Paris $110, Moscow $65, Berlin $92. Hotel value labels are light grey #D9D9D9 bold, placed above each column; Airbnb value labels are dark blue #00517A bold, placed above each column. Legend below the axis, centred: small grey square then 'Hotel', small blue square then 'Airbnb', bold dark grey. No highlighted points. Chart is not cropped and sits on white with no overlay. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark, grey, letter-spaced, bottom-left (a three-line lockup: KLEINER PERKINS, 2018, INTERNET TRENDS).

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background (#FFFFFF). Title band solid #00517A (dark teal-blue) spanning full width at top. Title text white #FFFFFF, Arial regular (sans-serif), two lines, large relative to slide height (about 4.4% of slide height per line, roughly 6% cap height). Chart title bold Arial, #3C444C, about 3.7% of slide height. Axis and category labels bold Arial, #3C444C for categories and #BFBFBF for y-axis values. Data labels bold Arial, about 2.6% of slide height; Hotel labels #D9D9D9, Airbnb labels #00517A. Source and page number in light grey Arial regular, about 1.3% and 1.5% of slide height. Column shapes are flat with no outlines, no corner radii, no shadows, no gradients. Gridlines thin light grey (#D9D9D9). Footer rule thin light grey.

X-axis has ten categories: Shelter, Taxes, Transportation, Food, Household Operations, Pensions* + Insurance, Healthcare, Entertainment, Apparel, Other**. Each category has three columns (left to right: light grey #D9D9D9, mid grey #BFBFBF, dark grey #A6A6A6) for three unlabelled years, except Transportation which has three coloured columns: 1972 navy #00517A labelled 14%, 1990 crimson #C82055 labelled 16%, 2017 green-teal #258B74 labelled 14%. Transportation highlighted: its category label is bold black and the other category labels are light grey. Legend below the plot: navy swatch 1972, crimson swatch 1990, teal swatch 2017, each in bold dark grey. Beneath the legend a row 'Total Expenditure' in italic with values $11K (1972), $31K (1990), $68K (2017). No photographs, icons or illustrations.

Source: Nerdwallet Study, March 2017. Washington D.C. included in Top 5 due to including of Baltimore MSA population. *Car commute costs include Gas (OPIS), Maintenance (Edmunds.com), Insurance (NerdWallet), & Parking (parkme.com). Note: Commute distances are from 2015 Brookings analysis. Uber data is based on a suburbs-to-city-center trip mirroring average commute distance for a metro. Data collected at peak commute times in February 2017. Cheapest Option (UberX, UberPOOL, etc.) selected for Uber costs.

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal header band across the top of the slide holds a two-line left-aligned white title that starts at about 1.9% from the left edge. Below it, a single centred bar chart sits in the middle of the slide with a bold two-line chart heading above it, and a centred legend beneath the category labels. The footer is separated by a thin light-grey rule and holds the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, a centred grey source note, and the page number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Chart: clustered vertical bar chart. Title: 'UberX / POOL vs. Personal Car* – Weekly Commute Costs', subtitle '5 Largest USA Cities, 2017'. Y-axis titled 'Weekly Cost' (USD per week), range $0 to $250 with light grey horizontal gridlines at $50 intervals ($0, $50, $100, $150, $200, $250). X-axis categories: New York City, Chicago, Washington D.C., Los Angeles, Dallas. Series 1 'Personal Car' (light grey #D9D9D9 bars, labels in dark grey #404040): New York City $218, Chicago $116, Washington D.C. $130, Los Angeles $89, Dallas $65. Series 2 'Uber' (dark teal #03527B bars, labels in teal): New York City $142, Chicago $77, Washington D.C. $96, Los Angeles $62, Dallas $181. Legend below the chart: grey square 'Personal Car', teal square 'Uber'. No points are specially highlighted; the Dallas Uber bar is the only Uber bar higher than its Personal Car bar. Bars are flat with no outlines or shadows. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark in grey, bottom left.

**Visuals**

Clustered column chart titled Relative Household Spending. Y axis labelled Annual Spend, USA, in percent, ranging 0% to 20% with gridlines at every 5%. Ten categories on the x axis: Shelter, Taxes, Transportation, Food, Household Operations, Pensions* + Insurance, Healthcare, Entertainment, Apparel, Other**, with labels angled about 45 degrees. Each category has three bars in the order 1972, 1990, 2017. Healthcare is the highlighted category: its label is bold black, and its three bars are coloured by year (1972 navy #03527B at 5%, 1990 crimson #C2185B at 5%, 2017 green #258B74 at 7%) with printed value labels 5%, 5% and 7% above them. The other nine categories use light grey bars for 1972 (#D9D9D9), mid grey for 1990 (#BFBFBF) and dark grey for 2017 (#A6A6A6), with no printed values; approximate values are Shelter about 11.8%, 15.4%, 16.8%; Taxes about 15.1%, 9.4%, 14.5%; Transportation about 14.3%, 16.3%, 13.5%; Food about 15.3%, 14.6%, 11.6%; Household Operations about 11.1%, 12.3%, 11.4%; Pensions* + Insurance about 6.6%, 8.2%, 10.1%; Entertainment about 6.3%, 4.5%, 4.2%; Apparel about 5.0%, 5.1%, 2.6%; Other** about 9.3%, 9.0%, 8.1%. Legend below the chart as three short horizontal swatches with bold labels 1972 (navy), 1990 (crimson) and 2017 (green), and a row beneath reading Total Expenditure in italic with $11K, $31K and $68K under the respective years. Logo at bottom left: Kleiner Perkins wordmark over 2018 INTERNET TRENDS in grey.

139

**Layout**

Three equal columns separated by thin vertical grey rules at about x 33% and x 66%, each with a bold centered two-line heading and an italic company name, a phone screenshot or photo in a black-bordered box, a bold chart caption and a small line chart beneath. The title sits left-aligned in a full-width blue band across the top. The source footnote is centered in the footer with the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left and the page number 139 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Three elements. (1) Left: phone screenshot of the Nurx app on a salmon-red header, showing an ORTHO TRI-CYLCLEN logo, a green progress bar, 'Ortho Tri-Cyclen / Request reviewed by doctor. / Jul 6 2017', 'New Message' and a message from Dr. Knox ('Hi Ashley, I just got off the phone with your pharmacy. They should be sending 2 packs of Ortho Tri-Cyclen...') with a bottom tab bar of Home, Messages, Orders, Profile; boxed with a thick black border. (2) Centre: photograph of a white wall-mounted medical signage board with blue headers and rows of text, shot at an angle with perspective from the left, cool grey-white lighting, boxed with thick black border. (3) Right: phone screenshot of the Cedar ABC Health System billing page showing 'Hi, Alice.', 'PATIENT Alice Montgomery', 'PROVIDER ABC Health', 'LAST VISIT November 20, 2017', 'NEXT BILL DUE Today', 'Total: $600.00', 'Your Payment Options', and a dark blue PAY TOTAL $600.00 button; boxed with thick black border. Charts: (a) Line chart 'Medical Interactions*', y-axis 'Interactions' 0 to 100K with gridlines at 50K and 100K, x-axis 2016, 2017, 2018, green (#2E8B6E approx) line rising from about 5K in 2016 to about 100K at the end of 2018 with small dips; no legend, no printed data labels. (b) Line chart 'Patients', y-axis 'Patients' 0 to 1,000K with gridlines at 500K and 1,000K, x-axis 2013, 2015, 2017, green line rising from near 0 in 2013 to about 880K in 2017, curving upward; no data labels. (c) Line chart '% of Collections**', y-axis '% of Collections' 0% to 100% with gridlines at 50% and 100%, x-axis 'Days' 0, 31, 60, 91, green line rising steeply from 0% at day 0 to about 55% at day 31, about 70% at day 60, about 80% at day 91 and about 84% at the end; no data labels.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF with a dark blue #00517A title band across the top. White content area with a full-width dark blue title band (#00517A) across the top 12.5% of the slide. Title in white regular Arial-like sans-serif at about 4.4% of slide height. Column headings in bold Arial sans-serif, dark slate #3C444C, about 3.7% of slide height, centered. Company names in italic Arial, #3C444C, about 3.0%. Chart captions bold Arial #3E464E at about 2.6%. Axis labels and tick labels bold Arial in light grey #BFBFBF at about 1.85%. Footnote in regular Arial #BFBFBF at about 1.3%. Page number regular Arial #A6A6A6 at about 1.5%. Vertical divider rules thin light grey. Phone and photo images have thick black borders with square corners and no shadows. Line charts use a single green stroke (#2E8B6E approx), thin gridlines in light grey. Logo text in grey, spaced capitals.

A thin footer rule sits near y 93%, with the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, a centred three-line source note, and the page number 143 at bottom right near x 96%.

**Visuals**

Line chart titled 'New Technology Proliferation Curves*' (bold). Y axis: 'Adoption, USA', 0% to 100%, gridlines at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, light grey. X axis: years 1900 to 2017, labels at 1900, 1915, 1930, 1945, 1960, 1975, 1990, 2005, 2017. No values are printed on the series, so all values are approximate. Series (legend order): Grid Electricity, yellow, about 10% in 1907 rising to about 68% by 1929 and about 99% by 1958, ending near 1960. Radio, brown, starts about 10% in 1923 and reaches about 96% by 1957 and about 97% by 1985. Refrigerator, dark blue, starts about 1% in 1925, about 72% in 1941, about 98% by 1966, and reaches 100% by about 1978. Automatic Transmission, black, starts 0% in 1939, about 36% in 1951, about 82% in 1961, and reaches 100% by about 1985. Internet, pink, starts about 10% in 1993, about 50% in 2001, about 81% in 2010 and about 88% in 2017. Social Media Usage, maroon, starts about 5% in 2005, about 21% in 2008, about 62% in 2014 and about 69% in 2017. Smartphone Usage, gold, starts about 35% in 2010, about 58% in 2014 and about 77% in 2017. Legend: twelve colour-coded line swatches in three rows, labels in grey. No highlighted points.

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with two-line white title left-aligned at the left margin (about 1.9% from the left). Below the band two chart panels sit side by side on white: a narrow log-scale scatter at left (about x 12-47%) and a dual-axis chart at right (about x 55-92%), each with a bold chart heading above it. A thin grey footer rule runs near the bottom with the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, a centred two-line source note, and the page number 145 at bottom right (about x 96%, y 95%).

**Visuals**

Two charts. Left chart: scatter plot titled '$1,000 of Computer Equipment'. Y axis is logarithmic, titled 'Calculations per Second', ranging 1.E-07 to 1.E+10 with one tick per decade; X axis runs 1900 to 2025 with ticks every 25 years (1900, 1925, 1950, 1975, 2000, 2025). Single series of green (#258B74) dots, with a dotted green trendline rising from about 1.E-07 near 1900 to about 1.E+08 near 2008. Labelled points: Analytical Engine (about 1.E-05 near 1837), IBM Tabulator (about 1.E-03 near 1928), BINAC (about 1.E+02 near 1950), IBM 1130 (about 1.E+01 near 1965), Sun 1 (about 1.E+06 near 1982), Pentium II PC (about 1.E+08 near 1997); the highest dot sits near 1.E+10 around 2008. No legend. Right chart: dual-axis plot titled 'Storage Price vs. Hard Drive Capacity'. Left axis 'Price per GB' is log scale from $0.01 to $10,000,000 (ticks $0.01, $0, $0.1, $1, $10, $100, $1,000, $10,000, $100,000, $1,000,000, $10,000,000). Right axis 'Hard Drive Storage Capacity' is log scale from 0.001GB to 10000GB (ticks 0.001GB, 0.01GB, 0.1GB, 1GB, 10GB, 100GB, 1000GB, 10000GB). X axis labelled 1956, 1987, 2017. Red (#C8184F-like) line series 'Price Per GB' falls from about $1,000,000 near 1960 to about $0.03 near 2015, with a flat section near $200,000 around 1969-1972 and a steep drop through 1980s. Green (#258B74) scatter series 'Capacity' with dots from about 0.001GB near 1956 rising to about 5,000,000 GB-equivalent points near 2016, with a dashed green trendline from about $0.04 near 1980 to the top-right near 10000GB. Legend at bottom: red line 'Price Per GB', green line 'Capacity'. No highlighted points. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark image at bottom left (390x92 px image, grey text on white).

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background. Title band in dark teal-blue #00517A across the top 12.5% of slide height with white text. 146

**Layout**

Full-width title band across the top of the slide, with the title left-aligned at about 2% from the left edge and set in two lines. A single centred line chart sits below the band, with its chart title centred above the plot and a horizontal legend centred beneath the x-axis. The footer has the Kleiner Perkins wordmark at bottom left, a centred source note in the bottom middle, and the page number right-aligned near the bottom right margin.

**Visuals**

Line chart titled Internet + Social Media – Global Penetration. Y-axis labelled Penetration, Global, in percent, ranging from 0% to 60% with gridlines every 10%. X-axis shows years 2009 to 2017 at one-year intervals, with no axis title. Series 1, Internet (crimson line, data labels shown): 2009 24% (printed); 2010 about 26.5%; 2011 about 29.7%; 2012 about 32.3%; 2013 about 35.5%; 2014 about 38.3%; 2015 about 41.5%; 2016 about 46.0%; 2017 49% (printed). Series 2, Social Media (navy line, data labels shown): 2010 14% (printed); 2011 about 17.5%; 2012 about 19.9%; 2013 about 22.3%; 2014 about 26.6%; 2015 about 29.6%; 2016 about 31.2%; 2017 33% (printed). Social Media has no 2009 point. Printed labels are the only values shown; the other points are estimates. Highlighted points are the labelled start and end points of each line. Legend below the plot: a short crimson line swatch labelled Internet and a short navy line swatch labelled Social Media, both in bold. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark, grey, bottom left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate style with a white background and a dark teal header band. Title text is white, regular weight, sans-serif (Arial-like), about 4.4% of slide height. Chart title is bold dark slate grey #3C444C, sans-serif, about 3.7% of slide height. Axis tick labels and year labels are bold light grey #BFBFBF, about 2.2% of slide height. Data labels are bold, about 2.6% of slide height, coloured to match their series. Body and source text is light grey #BFBFBF, about 1.3% of slide height. Lines are about 3 pt thick with round ends; gridlines are thin light grey #D9D9D9 horizontal rules. Accent colours: crimson #C82055 for Internet and navy #00517A for Social Media and the header band. Line chart titled 'Real GDP vs. Unemployment Rate, USA'. Left y-axis labelled 'Real GDP' from $0 to $18T with gridlines at $0, $6T, $12T, $18T. Right y-axis labelled 'Unemployment Rate' from 0% to 30% with matching labels 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%. X-axis years 1929 to 2017, labels every 10 years (1929, 1939, 1949, 1959, 1969, 1979, 1989, 1999, 2009, 2017). Series 1: Real GDP, solid dark blue line (about #00517A), rising from about $0.9T in 1929 to about $17T in 2017 (values approximate, not printed). Series 2: Unemployment Rate, solid red line (#C00000), peaking at about 25% around 1933, falling to about 2.9% near 1944 region dip, rising to about 9.7% near 1982, and ending at 3.9% in 2017 (labelled '3.9% Unemployment Rate (4/18)'). A horizontal dashed dark grey line (#3C444C) at about 5.8% across roughly 1945 to 2017 marks the 70-Year Average, labelled '5.8%' and '70-Year Average'. Legend centred below the axes: blue line 'Real GDP' and red line 'Unemployment Rate'. Gridlines light grey horizontal at the four value levels. Highlighted point: the red end label at 2017.

**Text**

Technology = Makes Freelance Work Easier to Find… / Freelance Workforce = 3x Faster Growth vs. Total Workforce / Has Technology Has Made It / Easier To Find Freelance Work? / 77% / 69% / Workforce Growth – / Freelance vs. Total / 100% / 110% / 108% / 106% / 104% / 102% / 100% / 75% / 50% / USA / Growth, / Workforce / % Responding Positively, USA / 2014 / 2015 / 2016 / 2017 / 2014 / 2015 / 2016 / 2017 / +8.1% / +2.5% / Total / Freelance / Source: ‘Freelancing in America: 2017’ survey conducted by Edelman Research, co-commissioned by / Upwork and Freelancers Union. **Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top (about 12.5% of slide height) carrying a two-line white left-aligned title with a left margin of about 1.9%. Below it two side-by-side line charts occupy the body, each with a bold dark grey centred two-line heading, separated by a thin vertical light grey divider at about x 50%. A thin light grey horizontal rule sits near y 93% above a footer: Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, centred three-line grey source note, and page number 163 at bottom right, right margin about 4%.

**Visuals**

Two line charts. (1) Left chart, title 'Has Technology Has Made It Easier To Find Freelance Work?'. Line chart, no legend. Y-axis titled '% Responding Positively, USA', range 50% to 100%, gridlines and tick labels at 50%, 75%, 100%. X-axis categories 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017. One navy series (#00517A) with labelled values 69% at 2014 and 77% at 2017; 2015 and 2016 values unlabelled, about 72% each. Endpoint labels are black bold. (2) Right chart, title 'Workforce Growth – Freelance vs. Total'. Line chart. Y-axis titled 'Workforce Growth, USA', range 100% to 110%, gridlines and tick labels every 2% (100%, 102%, 104%, 106%, 108%, 110%). X-axis categories 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017. Series 'Total' navy #00517A: 2014 100%, 2015 about 100.7%, 2016 about 101.9%, 2017 labelled +2.5% (about 102.5%). Series 'Freelance' crimson/magenta #C8175D: 2014 100%, 2015 about 102.0%, 2016 about 103.8%, 2017 labelled +8.1% (about 107.6%). Legend below the plot, centred: navy line then 'Total', magenta line then 'Freelance', bold dark grey labels. Endpoint labels: +8.1% in dark navy #00344E, +2.5% in grey #7F7F7F. Line widths about thick (roughly 4 px at slide scale), round caps. Logo images: Kleiner Perkins wordmark block at bottom left, grey.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white slide with a dark blue title band (#00517A) across the top. Title text white, regular weight sans-serif (Arial), about 4.4% of slide height. Chart headings bold dark slate grey #3E464E, about 3.3% of slide height; the left heading is bold italic, the right heading bold upright. Axis labels and year labels bold light grey #BFBFBF, about 2.2% of slide height. Data labels bold, black #000000 for 69% and 77%, navy #00344E for +8.1%, grey #7F7F7F for +2.5%, about 3.0% height. Footer source text regular light grey #BFBFBF about 1.3% height; page number grey #A6A6A6 about 1.5%. Lines: navy #00517A and crimson #C8175D, thick strokes; gridlines thin light grey #D9D9D9; vertical divider very thin light grey. No shadows, gradients, or corner radii.

**Layout**

A full-width dark blue title band across the top with a white two-line title left-aligned at a small left margin. Below it, a horizontal grey timeline arrow spans the middle with three year labels above it, and three equal-width boxed black-and-white photographs in a centred row beneath, each with a bold name and two centred description lines. A grey footer rule sits near the bottom, with the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, a centred source note, and the page number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Timeline diagram: a light grey (#DEDEDE) right-pointing block arrow runs from about x 19% to x 84.5% at y 23.7% to 32.1%, with three years in bold green (1955, 1960, 1965) above it. Three small grey (#808080) filled dots sit on the arrow's shaft at about x 25.8%, 36.3% and 62.6% (y about 27.9%), each joined by a thin vertical grey stem down to the top edge of the photo beneath it. Three black-and-white photographs: (1) Social Security: a 1950s computer room with several tall tape-drive cabinets along the back, two technicians standing at the cabinets, and a seated man in a suit at a desk in the foreground operating a console and a typewriter-style terminal; medium-wide framing, soft overhead light, grey and white tones, boxed with a thin black border. (2) NASA: a control room with long consoles and rows of equipment, a large wall clock on a pillar, two seated operators in the foreground and a standing man at the back, a ceiling of recessed fluorescent panels, grey and white tones, boxed with a thin black border. (3) IRS: a wide room with rows of tape-drive cabinets on the left, a central console with a monitor, a single seated operator chair in the right foreground, fluorescent light fixtures overhead, a dark herringbone-patterned floor, grey tones, boxed with a thin black border. The photos are not cropped, full-bleed or tinted. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark in grey letterspaced type at bottom left.

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background; a dark blue title band (#00517A) across the top 12.5% of the slide. Title text is white, regular-weight sans-serif (Arial-like), about 4.4% of slide height for the caps-height line. Year labels are bold sans-serif (Arial Bold) in green #31AF78, about 3.7% of slide height. Name labels are bold Arial in dark slate #3C444C, about 3.7%. Description text is regular Arial in #3C444C, about 2.4%. Source text is light grey #BFBFBF, about 1.3%. Page number is #A6A6A6, about 1.5%. Timeline arrow is flat #DEDEDE with no outline, no shadow. Dots and stems are flat #808080, stems about 2 px wide. Photos have thin black borders and no shadow or rounded corners. Footer rule is a thin pale grey line.

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top (about 12.5% of slide height) with a two-line left-aligned white title starting at about 1.9% from the left edge. A centred chart occupies the middle, with its title centred above the plot area, and a footer strip at the bottom holds the Kleiner Perkins logo at the far left, a centred three-line source note, and the page number at the right near the bottom edge. The chart is a single full-width area plot with a left y-axis and bottom x-axis, and labelled arrow callouts rise from the baseline.

**Visuals**

Chart: filled area chart titled 'Information Created Worldwide' with subtitle '(per IDC)'. Y-axis titled 'Zettabytes (ZB)', rotated vertically, range 0 to 180 ZB with labelled ticks every 20 (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160, 180); light grey horizontal gridlines at each tick. X-axis years 2004 to 2024E labelled every two years (2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018E, 2020E, 2022E, 2024E). Single series, grey area (#BFBFBF) under a rising curve from about 0 at 2004 to 163 ZB at 2025E; the curve is nearly flat until about 2010, then rises steeply. Labelled values: 2005 0.1 ZB; 2010 2 ZB, 9%; 2015 12 ZB, 9%; 2020E 47 ZB, 16%; 2025E 163 ZB, 36%. Each labelled point has a dark teal (#00517A) vertical arrow, arrowhead pointing up, from the baseline to just under the label; the arrows are at 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020E and 2025E. Legend: none; the axis caption 'Amount, % Structured' sits in light grey near the top left of the plot. Highlighted points: the five arrowed points. Logo at bottom left: 'KLEINER PERKINS / 2018 / INTERNET TRENDS' in grey letter-spaced sans-serif. No photographs.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Plain white background. Title band is solid dark teal blue #00517A with white Arial regular title text, about 4.4% of slide height per line. Chart title is Arial bold, dark slate #3C444C, about 3.3% of slide height; subtitle regular Arial about 3.0%. Axis tick labels, axis caption and x-axis years are Arial bold light grey #BFBFBF at about 2.2% of slide height. Data labels are Arial bold #3C444C at about 2.2%. Source footnote is Arial regular #BFBFBF at about 1.3%. Page number is Arial regular #A6A6A6 at about 1.5%. Shapes are flat: no shadows, gradients, rounded corners. Background white #FFFFFF. Header band solid #00517A (deep teal blue). Title text white #FFFFFF in a regular sans-serif (Arial-like, ArialMT), two lines, about 4.4% of slide height per line, not bold. **Text**

Smartphones = China @ #1 Worldwide OEM... / @ 40% vs. 0% Share Ten Years Ago...USA @ 15% vs. 3% / Worldwide New Smartphone Shipments by OEM Headquarters / 1.5B / 60% / 40% / 1.0B / Shipments / China OEM Share / Worldwide / 0.5B / 20% / 0% / 0 / 0% / 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 / China / USA / Korea / Other / % from China OEMs / KLEINER PERKINS / 2018 / INTERNET TRENDS / Source: Katy Huberty @ Morgan Stanley (3/18), IDC. **Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band fills the top 12.5% of the slide, holding a two-line left-aligned white title that starts about 1.9% from the left edge. Below it a single wide chart is centred in the middle of the slide, with its bold chart title centred above the plot area and a row of legend entries centred beneath the x-axis labels. A thin light grey footer rule sits near 93% of the height; the Kleiner Perkins logo is at bottom left, a centred source line runs along the footer, and the page number 219 sits at bottom right in the right margin.

**Visuals**

One combined chart: a stacked column chart with a line overlay, titled Worldwide New Smartphone Shipments by OEM Headquarters. Left value axis titled Worldwide Shipments, ticks 0, 0.5B, 1.0B, 1.5B (units: billion smartphones shipped per year). Right value axis titled China OEM Share, ticks 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%. Horizontal axis shows years 2007 to 2017. Stacks from bottom to top are China (red), USA (blue), Korea (grey), Other (mint). Estimated totals, marked about because no totals are printed: 2007 about 0.12B, 2008 about 0.15B, 2009 about 0.17B, 2010 about 0.31B, 2011 about 0.49B, 2012 about 0.72B, 2013 about 1.01B, 2014 about 1.30B, 2015 about 1.44B, 2016 about 1.47B, 2017 about 1.46B. Legend along the bottom: red square China, dark blue square USA, light grey square Korea, pale mint square Other, red line with label % from China OEMs. Light grey horizontal gridlines at 0.5B steps. The 0% and 40% labels are in bold red. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends lockup in grey lettering at bottom left, with a smaller wordmark image KLEINER PERKINS overlapping its upper part. Not cropped, no photographs or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, with a dark teal #00517A band across the top 12.5%. Plain white background with a dark teal header band #00517A. Title is white Arial regular, large, two lines. **Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide, with a two-line left-aligned white title inside it. Below, two equal columns sit centred at about 27% and 74% of the width, each with a bold centred heading, a regular subheading, a pair of phone screenshots framed in black, and a bold centred caption beneath. A thin light grey rule sits near the bottom at about 93% height, with the Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends logo bottom-left, a small grey source line centred and the page number 222 bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Two phone-app screenshot composites, each showing two side-by-side phone screens with thin black frames, no photographs. Left (Tencent, about 7.9% to 47.3% of width, 30.6% to 75.2% of height): left screen is the WeChat chat list with header 'WeChat (22)', a search icon and a plus icon on a dark grey bar, followed by rows Moments, Scan QR Code, Shake, People Nearby, Message in a Bottle, Games and Mini Program, each with a small coloured icon; bottom tab bar reads Chats (with red badge 22), Contacts, Discover (highlighted in green) and Me. Right screen is the WeChat Wallet page with status bar '11:05' and '68%' battery, header 'Me' and 'Wallet', a grey band with Money, Balance (¥50.00) and Cards, then 'Powered by Tencent' and a grid of Mobile Top Up, Wealth, QQ Coins, Utilities, Public Services, Card Repay and Tencent Charity, ending with 'Limited time promotion'. Right (Alibaba, about 55.7% to 92.4% of width, 30.2% to 75.1% of height): left screen is the Taobao home page with an orange header and search field, a red promotional banner reading 年度520特惠 with a pink handbag, a grid of round coloured category icons, and a product grid of clothing items with section labels; bottom tab bar has a Taobao icon. Right screen is the Alipay home page with a blue header and icons Scan, Pay, Collect, Pocket, followed by Phone Top-up, Card Repay, Utilities, My Packages, Yu'E Bao, Zhima Credit, Ant Farm, Ant Forest, City Service, Help Center, Ant Fortune and More, then a green tree illustration and red HOT envelope graphics. A smaller image (about 55.7% to 75.1% of width, 56.6% to 75.1% of height) overlaps the lower part of the Alibaba left screen. Screenshots are flat, straight-on, unlit UI captures; dominant colours are dark grey and white (WeChat), orange and red with white (Taobao), blue and white (Alipay).

### Slide 224

**Text**

China Internet Users = / More Willing to Share Data for Benefits vs. Other Countries per GfK / Would you share personal data (financial, driving records, etc.) / for benefits (e.g., lower cost, personalization, etc.)? / China / Mexico / Russia / Italy / Global / Brazil / USA / South Korea / Australia / UK / Spain / France / Canada / Germany / Netherlands / Japan / 0% / 10% / 20% / 30% / 40% / % of Global Respondents Very Willing to Share (6 or 7 on 7 Point Scale) / Source: GfK Survey (1/17). Note: n = 22K of internet users ages 15+. A scale of 1-7 were used to identify the level of agreement with the / following statement: “I am willing to share my personal data (health, financial, driving records, energy use, etc.) in exchange for benefits or / rewards like lower costs or personalized service” – using a scale where “1” means “don’t agree at all” and “7” means “agree completely.” / . / 223

**Layout**

Full-width title band across the top with two left-aligned white title lines inside a dark teal bar. Series, one bar each, values printed: China 38%, Mexico 30%, Russia 29%, Italy 28%, Global 27%, Brazil 26%, USA 25%, South Korea 20%, Australia 17%, UK 16%, Spain 16%, France 15%, Canada 14%, Germany 12%, Netherlands 12%, Japan 8%. Legend: none. Highlighted points: China bar in pure red #FF0000 with red bold label, Global bar in mint #A9E7CD with mint bold label, USA bar in blue #00689D with blue bold label; all other bars light grey #D9D9D9 with grey labels. Bar lengths are proportional to the printed values. Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark in grey at bottom left, a boxed image of 390 by 92 pixels.

Source: USA National Science Foundation analysis of National Bureau of Statistics (China), Government of Japan, UNESCO, OECD, National Center for Education Statistics, IPEDS, & National Center for Science /
Engineering data. Note: Data for the majority of the countries were collected under same OECD, EU, and UIS guidelines & field groupings in the ISCED-F are similar to fields used in China, a major degree producer.
Natural sciences include agricultural sciences; biological sciences; computer sciences; earth, atmospheric, and ocean sciences; & mathematics. EU-Top 8 for doctoral degrees includes UK / Germany / France / Spain /
Italy / Portugal / Romania / Sweden. EU-Top 8 for first university degrees includes UK / Germany / France / Poland / Italy / Spain / Romania / The Netherlands. The # of S&E doctorates awarded rose from about 8K in
2000 to more than 34K in 2014. Despite the growth in the quantity of doctorate recipients, some question the quality of the doctoral programs in China (Cyranoski et al. 2011). The rate of growth in doctoral degrees in
S&E and in all fields has considerably slowed starting in 2010, after an announcement by the Chinese Ministry of Education indicating that China would begin to limit admissions to doctoral programs & focus on quality
of graduate education (Mooney 2007). Also in China, first university degrees increased greatly in all fields, with a larger increase in non-S&E than in S&E fields. China experienced an increase of almost 1.2MM degrees
and up more than 400% from 2000 to 2014. China has traditionally awarded a large proportion of its first university degrees in engineering, but the percentage declined from 43% in 2000 to 33% in 2014.
KLEINER PERKINS
2018

**Layout**

Full-width blue title band across the top with two left-aligned white title lines, then a centred bold chart heading and italic subtitle, followed by two side-by-side line charts (First University on the left, Doctoral on the right) with a shared centred legend beneath them. A thin grey rule sits above a footer that holds the Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends logo at bottom left, a small centred-justified source and note block, and the slide number 227 at bottom right. Margins are about 1.6% on the left and right; the content sits on a single column grid with the two charts symmetrical around the centre.

**Visuals**

Two line charts side by side, sharing the same series and legend. Left chart: title First University, subtitle (Bachelor’s Equivalent); y-axis labelled First University Degrees, Selected Countries / Economies, ticks 0, 0.5MM, 1.0MM, 1.5MM (range 0 to about 1.5MM); x-axis years 2000 to 2014 in steps of 2. Series (values not printed, so estimates): China rises from about 0.28MM in 2000 to about 0.38MM by 2003, about 0.61MM in 2004, about 1.0MM in 2008, about 1.12MM in 2010, about 1.31MM in 2012 and about 1.45MM in 2014, a thick red line; USA rises from about 0.24MM in 2000 to about 0.38MM in 2014, a thick dark navy line; EU – Top 8 rises from about 0.40MM in 2000 to about 0.57MM in 2014, a thin peach line; Japan stays flat near about 0.13MM to 0.12MM, a thin mint line. Right chart: title Doctoral; y-axis labelled Doctorate Degrees, Selected Countries / Economies, ticks 0, 20K, 40K, 60K (range 0 to 60K); x-axis years 2000 to 2014. Series (estimates): China rises from about 7K in 2000 to about 16K in 2005, about 26K in 2008, about 29K in 2009, about 32K in 2014, thick red line; USA from about 17.5K in 2000, dipping to about 16.5K in 2002, about 25K in 2008, about 30K in 2014, thick navy line; EU – Top 8 from about 30.5K in 2000 to about 38K in 2006, about 44K in 2011, a peak of about 49.5K in 2013 and about 49K in 2014, thin peach line; Japan flat near about 6.5K to 6K, thin mint line. Legend centred below both charts: red line China, navy line USA, peach line EU – Top 8, mint line Japan. No highlighted points or markers; all lines are unfilled polylines.

The # of S&E doctorates awarded rose from about 8K in 2000 to more than 34K in 2014. Despite the growth in the quantity of doctorate recipients, some question the quality of the doctoral programs in China (Cyranoski et al. 2011). The rate of growth in doctoral degrees in S&E and in all fields has considerably slowed starting in 2010, after an announcement by the Chinese Ministry of Education indicating that China would begin to limit admissions to doctoral programs & focus on quality of graduate education (Mooney 2007). Also in China, first university degrees increased greatly in all fields, with a larger increase in non-S&E than in S&E fields. China experienced an increase of almost 1.2MM degrees and up more than 400% from 2000 to 2014. China has traditionally awarded a large proportion of its first university degrees in engineering, but the percentage declined from 43% in 2000 to 33% in 2014. **Layout**

**Visuals**

Chart: line chart titled E-Commerce % of Retail Sales (bold, dark grey #3E464E). Y-axis titled Share, labelled 0% to 25% in 5% steps, gridlines light grey at each 5% step. X-axis labelled every two years from 2003 to 2017, with data points at each labelled year. Eight series, each a line with markers absent: Korea (thin, teal #1AA7B8), UK (thin, orange-brown #C0700F), China (thick, dark red #C00000, the highlighted series, roughly 4 points thick), USA (thin, dark blue #00558A), Germany (thin, gold #E0A526), Japan (thin, sage green #7FB08A), France (thin, slate grey-blue #8A9BB0), Brazil (thin, pale cyan #7FCBD6). No individual values are printed, so the values below are estimates marked about. China: about 0.1% in 2003, 0.1% in 2005, 0.1% in 2007, 0.2% in 2008, 0.3% in 2009, about 1% in 2010, about 2.5% in 2011, about 4.3% in 2012, about 6.5% in 2013, about 9.8% in 2014, about 13.8% in 2015, about 17% in 2016, about 20.3% in 2017. Korea: about 4.1% in 2003, about 5.8% in 2006, about 8.9% in 2008, about 10.3% in 2011, about 12.7% in 2014, about 18.8% in 2017. Brazil: about 1.4% in 2003, about 3.2% in 2011, about 6.3% in 2017. Legend: horizontal row below the x-axis, each entry a short coloured line then a bold black label in the order Korea, UK, China, USA, Germany, Japan, France, Brazil; the China line sample is thicker. Highlighted point: the China line end at 2017 is emphasised by its thick dark red stroke. Logos: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends lockup (grey) at bottom left, Hillhouse red square logo with black Hillhouse Capital wordmark at bottom right.

### Slide 255

**Text**

China E-Commerce = Strong Growth +28% Y/Y… / Mobile = 73% of GMV / China B2C E-Commerce Gross Merchandise Value / $600B / 300% / B2C E-Commerce GMV, China / $400B / 200% / Mobile Growth Y/Y / $200B / 100% / $0 / 0% / 2013 / 2014 / 2015 / 2016 / 2017 / Desktop / Mobile / Mobile Growth Y/Y / Source: iResearch. Note: Assumes constant USD / RMB rate = 6.9. / KLEINER PERKINS / 2018 / INTERNET TRENDS / Hillhouse / Capital / 254

**Layout**

A full-width dark-blue title band sits across the top of the slide, with the two-line title left-aligned inside it. Below, a centred chart title sits above a combo chart that fills the middle of the slide, with a bottom legend row. A thin grey rule separates the footer, which holds a left-aligned Kleiner Perkins logo, a centred grey source line, and a right-aligned Hillhouse Capital logo with the page number 254 beside it.

**Visuals**

Combo chart titled China B2C E-Commerce Gross Merchandise Value. Left y-axis: B2C E-Commerce GMV, China, in US dollars billions, range $0 to $600B, gridlines at $200B, $400B and $600B. Right y-axis: Mobile Growth Y/Y, in percent, range 0% to 300%, labels at 100%, 200% and 300%. X-axis categories: 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017. Stacked columns: Desktop (bottom segment, dark blue #00517A) and Mobile (top segment, green #258B74). No values are printed on the bars, so these are estimates: Desktop about $90B, $120B, $128B, $119B, $131B for 2013 to 2017; Mobile segment tops about $106B, $181B, $286B, $374B, $481B for 2013 to 2017. Line series Mobile Growth Y/Y in crimson #C2185B, about 297% in 2014, about 158% in 2015, about 61% in 2016, about 36% in 2017; no point is plotted for 2013. Legend below the axis, left to right: Desktop (dark blue swatch), Mobile (green swatch), Mobile Growth Y/Y (crimson line). No highlighted points. Logos: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends logo at bottom left, Hillhouse Capital logo (red square with white HILLHOUSE mark and black wordmark) at bottom right.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Plain white background. Title band is a solid dark teal-blue rectangle #00517A with white title text in Arial regular, about 4.4% of slide height per line, about 6.8% line pitch. Chart title is Arial bold in charcoal #3E464E, about 3.7% of slide height. Axis labels and axis titles are Arial bold in light grey #BFBFBF, about 2.6% of slide height. Legend labels are Arial bold black #000000, about 2.2%. Source line is Arial regular grey #BFBFBF, about 1.3%. Page number is Arial regular #A6A6A6, about 1.5%. Gridlines are thin light grey horizontal lines. Bars are flat with no corners, shadows or gradients. The Mobile Growth line is about 2.5 pt wide with round joins. Hillhouse logo red #D7001F.

Bottom half: a black-and-white floor plan of the store (outline walls, four rectangular fixtures in the middle, a stair or counter at the bottom) with a blue-to-green-to-yellow-to-red heat map overlay, with red hotspots at top-left, centre-right, bottom-left and bottom-right and a small green-yellow spot in the centre. (2) RFID shoe pair, centre column: a pink ballet flat with beaded mauve and white pattern on the toe, photographed on white, at about x 40.6%, y 33.0%, w 19.5%, h 17.0%, with no box; below it a black pointed-toe kitten-heel slingback with an ankle strap and buckle, photographed on white, at about x 42.2%, y 57.1%, w 18.2%, h 20.2%. Values: 138 fittings / 37 sales / 27% conversion (pink flat); 168 fittings / 5 sales / 3% conversion (black heel); no chart axes, legend or highlighted points. A thin light-grey horizontal divider sits between the two shoes at about y 77.9%. (3) 3D foot scan, right column: a white floor-standing scanning robot with an orange-rimmed circular platform at its base, a grey speaker grille and an orange-accented top, overlapping four smartphone screenshots: top-left an orange gradient screen with a white line-drawn foot outline and the text PASSPORT; top-right a white screen with a grid of small size and measurement fields and two foot icons at the bottom; bottom-right a white screen with an orange circle showing a foot and a block of small Chinese text and an orange button. The composite sits at about x 68.8%, y 32.0%, w 23.5%, h 47.7%, cut-out with no box and with soft shadows.

### Slide 267

**Text**

Slack (2013) = Pioneered…
Enterprise-Grade Product With Consumer Look & Feel...
When you want something really bad,
you will put up with a lot of flaws.
But if you do not yet know you want something,
your tolerance will be much lower.
That’s why it is especially important for us to build a
beautiful, elegant and considerate piece of software.
Every bit of grace, refinement, & thoughtfulness
on our part will pull people along.
Every petty irritation will stop them &
give the impression that it is not worth it.
- Stewart Butterfield, Slack Founder / CEO (2013)
266

A full-width navy header band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide with a two-line left-aligned title inset about 1.9% from the left edge. Below it, a centred quotation block of italic body lines fills the middle of the slide, with a right-aligned bold attribution line near the bottom, a thin light-grey rule above a footer, the Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends logo at bottom left, and the page number 266 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

One logo: the Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark in small light-grey letterspaced capitals at bottom left, occupying about 18.3% by 6.2% of the slide, with the words KLEINER PERKINS on the first line, 2018 in the centre on the second, and INTERNET TRENDS on the third. No photographs, charts or diagrams.

**Layout**

Two side-by-side ranked tables fill the middle of the slide, each with a 'Government Debt' super-header over sub-columns '% of GDP' and '2017 ($B)', with a left column of country names; the left table is ranks 1-10 and the right table ranks 11-20. A full-width navy title band sits across the top, title left-aligned at about 2.4% from the left edge. The Kleiner Perkins logo is bottom-left, the source footnote is centred in the footer zone, and the page number is bottom-right at about 95.8% x.

**Visuals**

Table (no chart). Left table columns: Country, % of GDP, 2017 ($B). Rows: Japan 240% $12,317; Greece 180 403; Lebanon 152 80; Italy 133 2,798; Portugal 126 301; Singapore 111 362; USA 108 20,939 (row set in bold crimson #C82055 with bold 7) label); Jamaica 107 16; Cyprus 106 24; Belgium 104 561. Right table columns: Country, % of GDP, 2017 ($B). Rows: Egypt 101% $199; Spain 99 1,412; France 97 2,730; Jordan 96 39; Bahrain 91 31; Canada 90 1,482; UK 89 2,532; Mozambique 88 12; Ukraine 86 92; Yemen 83 30. Rules: a black horizontal line under each 'Government Debt' header (left about 22.4% to 48.4% x at 28.5% y; right about 72.3% to 96.3% x at 28.5% y) and a black line under each 'Country' header row spanning each table (left 5.1% to 48.4% x, right 50.8% to 96.3% x, at 32.5% y). Logo: Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends wordmark in grey, bottom-left, two images (a 390 by 92 px block and a 287 by 19 px line). No photographs or illustrations.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Plain white slide with a dark teal-blue title band across the top 12.5% of the height. Title text is white regular sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica-like), about 4.4% of slide height, with the superscript 'th' set smaller. Table headers 'Government Debt' and 'Country' are bold dark slate #3C444C at about 3.3% of slide height; sub-headers '% of GDP' and '2017 ($B)' are bold light grey #D9D9D9 at about 2.6%. Table body is regular Arial in #3C444C at about 3.5% of slide height; the USA row is bold crimson #C82055. Footnote is light grey #BFBFBF regular at about 1.3%; page number #A6A6A6 at about 1.5%. A thin light grey rule (#D9D9D9-ish, about 0.1% height) separates the footer at about 92.9% height. No shadows, gradients or rounded corners.
