**Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide with a two-line left-aligned white title inset about 1.9% from the left edge. Below it, a stacked-bar chart with its title centred above occupies the left and centre of the slide, with a bordered black-outlined change box in the right column (x 78 to 93.6%). Legend sits in two rows under the chart. A thin grey rule runs across the bottom at about y 93% with the Kleiner Perkins 2018 Internet Trends logo lower left, source notes centred in the footer and the page number 286 at lower right (x 95.8%).

**Visuals**

Chart 1: combined stacked-bar and line chart titled 'USA Expenses by Category'. Left axis 'US Expenses' 0% to 100% in 20% steps; right axis 'USA 10Y Treasury Yield' 0% to 10% in 2% steps. Two stacked bars, each with a total above it. 1987 bar, total $1.0T, segments bottom to top: Entitlements / Mandatory 42% (green #31AF78), Defense 28% (blue #00689D), Non-Defense Discretionary 16% (cyan #02B5CC), Net Interest Cost 14% (crimson #C82055). 2017 bar, total $4.0T, segments bottom to top: Entitlements / Mandatory 63% (green), Defense 15% (blue), Non-Defense Discretionary 15% (cyan), Net Interest Cost 7% (crimson). Segment labels are white bold centred in each segment. Yellow line (#FFC000-like) for 10 Year Treasury Yield, daily series from 12/31/86 to 12/31/17 on the right axis; values not printed, about 7.5% at the start, about 9.5% near the 1987 peak, about 4% near 2010 and about 1.7% at the end of 2017. A thin green straight line (#31AF78) runs from the top of the 1987 green segment (about 42%) up to the top of the 2017 green segment (about 63%), with no label. Legend below the chart: green square Entitlements / Mandatory, blue square Defense, yellow line 10 Year Treasury Yield, cyan square Non-Defense Discretionary, crimson square Net Interest Cost. Box at right: a black-outlined rectangle containing the heading '1987 → 2017 Change' (underlined) and five values. Magenta (#C82055) arrow connectors run from the Debt* entry (top) down the left side of the box to the Net Interest Cost entry, with arrowheads pointing right at each entry. Photograph/illustration: none.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, with a dark teal #00517A header band across the top 12.5%. Clean corporate-report look. White background (#FFFFFF). Header band #00517A (dark teal-blue) with white title text. Chart title and labels dark grey #3C444C in bold Arial-style sans-serif. Axis tick labels and axis titles light grey #BFBFBF bold sans-serif. Body and legend text dark grey #3C444C bold sans-serif. Title is regular-weight Arial-like sans-serif, about 4.4% of slide height for each line; chart title about 3.7%; body labels about 2.2%; footer text about 1.3%. Accent colours: green #31AF78, blue #00689D, cyan #02B5CC, crimson #C82055, yellow line #FFC000-like. Shape styles: flat bars with no outlines, light grey gridlines at 20% steps, black 1pt outline on the change box, square corners, no shadows, no gradients.

### Slide 288

**Text**

…USA Entitlements = / Medicare + Medicaid Driving Most Spending Growth… / USA Entitlements by Category / 1987 Entitlements* = / $349B / 35% of Expenses / 2017 Entitlements* = / $2.2T / 56% of Expenses / 30% / 24% / 20% / 20% / 15% / USA Mandatory Entitlements / 9% / 10% / 8% / 7% / 4% / 3% / 0% / Social Security / Medicare / Medicare / Medicaid / Medicaid / Income Security / 1987 / 2017 / 287 / Source: Congressional Budget Office, White House Office of Management and Budget. *1987 Income Security programs / defined as Food Stamps + SSI + Family Support + Child Nutrition + Earned Income Tax Credit + Other. 2017 Income / Security defined as Earned Income Tax Credit + SNAP + SSI + Unemployment + Family Support + Child Nutrition. In / 2017, there was an additional ~$200MM in mandatory spending, including Veterans’ pensions & ~$73MM in 1987. Also in the logo lockup: KLEINER PERKINS / 2018 / INTERNET TRENDS

**Layout**

A full-width solid navy title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide with a two-line left-aligned white title inset about 1.9% from the left edge. Below it, a centred chart heading and a pair of centred 1987 and 2017 summary captions sit above a single clustered column chart occupying roughly x 18% to 88% and y 33% to 90%, with the chart area spanning the middle of the slide. A hairline rule separates the chart from a footer band holding the Kleiner Perkins logo at bottom left, a four-line centred source note, and the page number 287 at bottom right near x 96%.

**Visuals**

Clustered column chart titled 'USA Entitlements by Category', vertical axis labelled 'USA Mandatory Entitlements' (rotated 90 degrees, grey bold) with percentage ticks 0%, 10%, 20%, 30% (0% to 30% range, unit percent of expenses), horizontal light-grey gridlines at 10%, 20% and 30%. Categories on the horizontal axis: Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, Income Security. Series 1987 (pale cyan #C3F8FE for Social Security and Income Security, navy #00517A for Medicare and Medicaid) with labelled values: Social Security 20%, Medicare 7%, Medicaid 3%, Income Security 4%. Series 2017 (pale pink #F7CFDC for Social Security and Income Security, crimson #C82055 for Medicare and Medicaid) with labelled values: Social Security 24%, Medicare 15%, Medicaid 9%, Income Security 8%. Legend at bottom centre: navy swatch labelled 1987 and crimson swatch labelled 2017. Above the chart, a white block arrow with thin black outline points right between the two captions. No points are specially highlighted.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF background, with a navy #00517A title band across the top 12.5% of the slide. Clean corporate look on a white background. Title band is solid navy #00517A with white title text in a regular-weight sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica style) at about 4.4% of slide height per line. Chart heading is bold dark slate #3C444C sans-serif (Arial Bold style) at about 3.7% of slide height. Captions: 1987 in navy #00517A regular and bold values in navy; 2017 in crimson #C82055 regular and bold values in crimson, about 2.6% of slide height. Axis tick labels and category labels are bold light grey #BFBFBF for the outer categories and dark slate #3C444C overlapping duplicates; data labels are bold dark grey #404040 at about 2.2% of slide height. Gridlines are thin light grey. Bars are flat rectangles with no shadows or gradients and no rounded corners. Footer source text is light grey #BFBFBF regular at about 1.3% of slide height. Page number is grey #A6A6A6.

### Slide 294

**Text**

Global Industry Classification System (GICS)
(Slides 39 / 41 / 42)
GICS is a four-tiered, hierarchical industry classification system. It consists of 11 sectors, 24 industry groups, 68 industries and 157 sub-industries.
The GICS methodology is widely accepted as an industry analytical framework for investment research, portfolio management and asset allocation.
Companies are classified quantitatively and qualitatively. Each company is assigned a single GICS classification at the sub-industry level according to
its principal business activity. MSCI and S&P Global use revenues as a key factor in determining a firm’s principal business activity. Earnings and
market, however, are also recognized as important and relevant
information for classification purposes.
Global industry coverage is comprehensive and precise. The classification system is comprised of over 50,000 trading securities across 125 countries,
covering approximately 95% of the world’s equity market capitalization.
Company classifications are regularly reviewed and maintained. Specialized teams from two major index providers — MSCI and S&P Global — have
defined review procedures, refined over nearly 15 years.
Each sector includes the following industries:
• Energy = Energy Equipment & Services, Oil, Gas & Consumables Fuels
• Materials = Chemicals, Construction Materials, Containers & Packaging, Metals & Mining, Paper & Forest Products
• Industrials = Aerospace & Defense, Building Products, Construction & Engineering, Electrical Equipment, Industrial Conglomerates, Machinery,
Trading Companies & Distributors, Commercial Services & Suppliers, Professional Services, Air Freight & Logistics, Airlines, Marine, Road & rail,
Transportation Infrastructure
• Consumer Discretionary = Auto Components, Automobiles, Household Durables, Leisure Products, Textiles, Apparel & Luxury Goods, Hotels,
Restaurants & Leisure, Diversified Consumer Services, Media, Distributors, Internet & Direct Marketing Retail, Multiline Retail, Specialty Retail
• Consumer Staples =Food & Staples Retailing, Beverages, Food Products, Tobacco, Household Products, Personal Products
• Healthcare = Healthcare Equipment & Supplies, Healthcare Providers & Services, Healthcare Technology, Biotechnology, Pharmaceuticals, Life
Sciences Tools & Services
• Financials = Commercial Banks, Thrifts & Mortgage Finance, Diversified Financial Services, Consumer Finance, Capital Markets, Mortgage Real
Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), Insurance
• Information Technology = Internet Software & Services, IT Services, Software, Communications Equipment, Computers & Peripherals, Electronic
Equipment & Instruments, Semiconductors & Semiconductors Equipment
• Telecommunication Services = Diversified Telecommunication Services, Wireless Telecommunication Services
• Utilities = Electric Utilities, Gas Utilities, Multi-Utilities, Water Utilities, Independent Power & Renewable Electricity Producers
• Real Estate = Equity Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), Real Estate Management & Development
Source: MSCI, S&P 500
